2_Introduction: PSCs with a PCE of 25.3859%, a JSC of 26.616 mA/cm², a VOC of 1.1878 V and an FF of 80.2987% are demonstrated. Commencing with a Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 solution at 1.65 mol/L, the perovskite precursor was meticulously formulated. The precursor solution was deposited on the substrate and spin-coated with a two-step spin-coating procedure: 1000 rpm for 5 s and 5500 rpm for 30 s. During the last 15 s of the second step, 150 µL of chlorobenzene (CB) was added as the antisolvent. Afterwards, the perovskite film was annealed at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-performance perovskite solar cell arises from a tightly coupled interplay between compositional engineering, kinetic control of crystallization, and intrinsic defect suppression—despite the absence of exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators in the reported protocol, the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ formulation inherently leverages A-site cation synergy to stabilize the photoactive α-phase: FA⁺ provides lattice robustness and optimal tolerance factor (~0.98), MA⁺ enhances crystallinity and charge-carrier mobility, while Cs⁺ suppresses halide vacancy formation and mitigates thermal/phase instability, collectively reducing non-radiative recombination centers at grain boundaries and surfaces; the precisely tuned precursor concentration (1.65 mol/L) ensures sufficient nucleation density without excessive supersaturation, while the two-step spin-coating—initial low-speed wetting (1000 rpm, 5 s) followed by rapid dewetting and crystal growth under high shear (5500 rpm, 30 s)—enables uniform film formation and controlled grain coalescence, with antisolvent quenching (150 µL chlorobenzene introduced at 15 s into the second step) critically arresting intermediate solvate phase evolution and promoting instantaneous nucleation of phase-pure perovskite, thereby minimizing PbI₂ residuals and suppressing trap-state formation at the nanoscale; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 15 min drives complete solvent removal, facilitates iodide redistribution, relieves lattice strain, and heals point defects—evidenced implicitly by the exceptional photovoltaic parameters which reflect suppressed bulk and interfacial recombination, efficient charge extraction, and minimal voltage losses—culminating in a PCE of 25.3859%, a JSC of 26.616 mA/cm², a VOC of 1.1878 V and an FF of 80.2987%.
